method: Source and test-body analysis only. All eight assigned source files and four local suites fully read; native shared implementation and relevant complete test bodies are explicitly bounded. No application, model, test, install or network execution.

entries.title: Evaluation runner, explicit model defaults and separate test configuration
entries.source: ice:packages/evals/scripts/run-evals.mjs:1-98; ice:packages/evals/src/ice-harness.ts:28-56; ice:packages/evals/package.json:1-21; ice:packages/evals/vitest.config.ts:1-21; ice:packages/evals/vitest.test.config.ts:1-15; ice:vitest.base.ts:1-29; ice:package.json:37; ice:packages/evals/test/ice-harness.test.ts:1-35; rust:Cargo.toml:1-24; rust:crates/ice-harness/Cargo.toml:1-43.
entries.what: A separate eval command chooses a default provider/model, launches only model-backed eval files, and keeps local unit tests distinct from those potentially authenticated runs.
entries.mechanism:
The runner gives explicit CLI provider/model values precedence over environment defaults and forwards other arguments to Vitest. A harness may override that default with its own model. The runner and harness validate selection at different points, so launching without a default is allowed only when the executed harnesses supply their own models.

The root npm eval script forwards to the private @zykairotis/ice-evals workspace. run-evals.mjs accepts --provider value, --model value and their = forms; repeated values overwrite earlier values. Separate-form values must be nonempty and must not start with '-'. After trimming, the presence of either CLI selector requires both CLI values; a missing CLI half is not filled from the environment. Without any CLI selector, trimmed ICE_PROVIDER and ICE_MODEL must either both exist or both be absent. All other arguments are retained in encounter order. There is no special end-of-options escape in this parser, so recognized selectors after a literal '--' are still consumed (ice:packages/evals/scripts/run-evals.mjs:16-63).

ICE_EVAL_ARTIFACT_DIR is resolved relative to the package root when truthy; otherwise the runner creates .eval/<ISO timestamp with colons replaced>_<UUID>. It creates the directory recursively with requested mode0700, prints the selected default and artifact location, then invokes process.execPath with Vitest's installed vitest.mjs, 'run', '--config', 'vitest.config.ts' and forwarded arguments. cwd is the eval package, stdio is inherited and the environment is copied with the resolved artifact path. Both model defaults are installed together or both removed. Spawn errors are thrown; a null child status becomes exit1, otherwise the child status is propagated. The runner does not parse authentication or independently resolve the chosen model (ice:packages/evals/scripts/run-evals.mjs:8-15; ice:packages/evals/scripts/run-evals.mjs:65-98).

resolveModelSelection uses explicitModel.provider/id via nullish fallback to environment fields, then trims and requires both. An explicit empty string therefore rejects rather than falling back. The local test suite covers explicit precedence, trimming and incomplete selections; it does not execute the runner or a model. Eval configuration runs src/**/*.eval.ts in Node with fileParallelism=false, testTimeout120000, hookTimeout30000, the eval afterEach setup, the external vitest-evals reporter and the local reporter. The separate unit-test configuration selects test/**/*.test.ts. Both use the monorepo source aliases, with an explicit coding-agent index alias; package metadata pins vitest-evals0.15.0 and Vitest4.1.9. Compiler configuration is noEmit/NodeNext through the shared strict ES2022 base. These are source configuration facts, not an assertion that dependencies were installed or tests ran.
entries.interfaces: Command: root npm run eval -- [--provider P --model M] [Vitest arguments]. Environment: ICE_PROVIDER, ICE_MODEL, ICE_EVAL_ARTIFACT_DIR. createIceCodingAgentHarness({name?,model?:{provider,id},noTools?,transformSystemPrompt?,output?}); default harness name ice-coding-agent. Paths: packages/evals/.eval/<timestamp>_<UUID>, runner override resolved relative to package root, src/**/*.eval.ts, test/**/*.test.ts.
entries.dependency_text: Model catalog lookup and authentication are performed later by MISC-041 through AI-002 and SESSION-028. This entry owns eval-only command/default selection rather than the normal CLI's model parser.
entries.rust: The native workspace and ice-harness crate are real Rust runtime/test packages, but their inspected manifests contain no eval package/target or wrapper for these model defaults, selectors and artifact runner. The bounded full crate search for createIceCodingAgentHarness, vitest-evals, ICE_EVAL_ and comparative eval/report names found no implementation. This is absence of the described eval runner in the inspected repository surface, not absence of native tests or a statement about external tooling. Native deterministic tests are credited in MISC-041 and MISC-048.
entries.port: Add an explicit opt-in eval executable or developer command with the exact selector precedence, forwarding, child exit and artifact-directory contract. Reuse the existing model/auth catalog, expose the final selected provider/model to each harness and keep deterministic tests separate from model-backed suites. Reproduce the checked-in runner's pair validation and explicit-empty behavior; if a native command adopts conventional '--' parsing, record that deliberate compatibility difference. Port the four source-read model-selection cases and add future runner tests for equals/separate forms, partial CLI selection and child failures.
entries.priority_reason: Required to run repeatable opt-in model evaluations without conflating them with ordinary unit tests.

entries.title: Isolated eval-session construction, prompt transformation and sequential reload steps
entries.what: Each harness run creates a fresh temporary project, agent directory and persistent session, then executes a string prompt or ordered prompt/reload program with a selectable output projection.
entries.mechanism:
Every run uses a fresh session and workspace while retaining the application's normal model authentication path. Optional prompt transformation sees the complete initial system prompt and is applied through a resource reload. Prompt and reload steps then execute sequentially, and the output callback sees the live final session before cleanup.

The timer and initial abort check precede model selection. ModelRuntime.create() is called with its normal defaults before the temporary root exists; getModel(provider,id) must return a model or the run rejects with 'Eval model not found: provider/id'. Only then does mkdtemp create an ice-eval- directory under the OS temp directory. workspace and agent children are created in parallel. createAgentSessionServices receives cwd, agentDir, that model runtime and SettingsManager.inMemory(); it does not replace normal model credentials with a temporary credential store. A resourceLoader systemPromptOverride closure is installed only when a transform was supplied. SessionManager.create uses the workspace and a sibling sessions directory, and its session ID is immediately placed in the 'runId' artifact. createAgentSessionFromServices selects the resolved model, thinkingLevel='off', and forwards noTools without changing its schema (ice:packages/evals/src/ice-harness.ts:115-151).

The transform callback is synchronous and receives evalSession.systemPrompt. Its returned string must have a nonempty trim; the original returned string, including intentional whitespace, remains the override. evalSession.reload() applies it. The harness then rejects any nonempty initial extension-path list, which asserts starting isolation before the test can create resources. It does not assert that the entire environment or model credential state is empty (ice:packages/evals/src/ice-harness.ts:153-168).

A string input becomes one prompt step; array steps retain order. Prompt steps call the stricter completion adapter in MISC-043. Every other branch in the typed prompt/reload union invokes reload; there is no additional runtime discriminator validation in this loop. Reloads may occur before the first prompt or after the last prompt, but at least one prompt must set response. The final response is the last prompt's returned text, even if a later reload changes session resources. When options contains an output property, its callback is awaited with {response,session}; otherwise the string is returned. The adapter's generic restricts custom output to JsonValue, while actual external createHarness normalization is a dependency boundary rather than locally implemented JSON validation (ice:packages/evals/src/ice-harness.ts:169-180; ice:packages/evals/src/ice-harness.ts:246-259).
entries.interfaces: IceCodingAgentInput = string | Array<{type:'prompt',content:string}|{type:'reload'}>. Isolation layout: <tmp>/ice-eval-*/workspace, agent, sessions. Options: model selection, noTools, transformSystemPrompt(defaultPrompt), async or sync output({response,session}); output callback executes before snapshot/disposal/removal. Artifact 'runId' is the native session ID.
entries.dependency_text: AI-002 owns model runtime/catalog behavior; SESSION-028 owns SDK service/session construction and SESSION-035 owns resource reload. This entry adds the evaluation-specific construction and sequence policy without recounting those implementations.
entries.rust: AgentHarness::create genuinely builds a native harness over a supplied Session, providers, tools, settings and resource configuration (rust:crates/ice-harness/src/agent_harness.rs:682-810). The complete inspected native harness_with_options helper constructs a FauxProvider, read/write/bash tools, InMemoryExecutionEnv and InMemorySessionStorage, then calls that constructor (rust:crates/ice-harness/tests/harness_run_e2e.rs:51-128). These are reusable isolated deterministic building blocks. They are not the application-session adapter that allocates real temporary project/agent/session directories, loads normal selected credentials, transforms the complete prompt, supports explicit reload steps and invokes an arbitrary JSON output projection. No native comparative eval wrapper was found in the bounded inventory.
entries.port: Build the eval adapter over the real application-session services and native harness, keeping model runtime resolution outside the temporary project settings. Allocate a scoped temporary root and explicit session storage, disable thinking for the baseline contract, forward tool policy, preserve transform-then-reload ordering and verify the initial extension set. Run prompt/reload steps in order and invoke the output projection while session/files still exist. Preserve the native deterministic in-memory helper for unit tests; use the real temporary project path when evaluating extension/resource authoring. Reuse SDK/reload implementations rather than replacing them with eval-specific mocks.
entries.priority_reason: Model comparisons require equivalent fresh application sessions and explicit reload behavior; native unit-test isolation alone does not provide that workflow.

entries.title: Eval cancellation, snapshot-before-disposal and cleanup error aggregation
entries.what: A run connects the evaluation signal to session abort, preserves the session JSONL while it still exists, attempts every cleanup operation, and reports cleanup failures without silently losing a primary run error.
entries.mechanism:
Abort is connected to the live session after construction and any initial prompt transformation. Cleanup then snapshots the session before disposing it and removing the temporary root. Failure reporting distinguishes the original run failure from later snapshot, disposal and removal errors.

The signal is checked before model/runtime work, after service creation, immediately after the abort listener is installed and before each prompt. The listener is once-only and memoizes evalSession.abort() in abortPromise. The inner finally removes the listener and awaits that promise if it was created. Initial transform/reload precedes listener installation; ordinary reload steps have no additional per-step throwIfAborted call. There is no final signal check after the output projection or usage collection. Therefore this source must not be described as a single enclosing cancellation race or as cancelling every setup phase immediately. An abortPromise rejection is an exception from the inner finally and becomes the caught run error (ice:packages/evals/src/ice-harness.ts:115-165; ice:packages/evals/src/ice-harness.ts:169-210).

The protected try begins only after model lookup and mkdtemp succeed. Failures before that boundary reject directly; no created session exists there. Within the try, all failures become an outcome object. If a SessionManager exists, its session file path is checked and the existing UTF-8 file is read into artifact 'iceSessionJsonl'. Missing or nonexistent files produce no snapshot. Snapshot errors are collected, then session.dispose() is attempted synchronously, then rm(root,{recursive:true,force:true}) is awaited. Both later attempts occur even when an earlier cleanup operation failed. The source has no explicit ModelRuntime disposal operation (ice:packages/evals/src/ice-harness.ts:208-232).

If the run failed and cleanup did not, rethrow the original value unchanged. If both failed, throw AggregateError([originalError,...cleanupErrors], 'Agent run failed and cleanup also failed.'). On a successful run, one cleanup error is thrown directly and multiple errors produce AggregateError(cleanupErrors,'Agent cleanup failed.'). Only a fully successful outcome returns timings.totalMs, measured from before model setup through completed cleanup. Failed paths do not construct this successful timing payload. The four local unit suites do not exercise cancellation/disposal failure combinations; these are direct source contracts, not executed test results.
entries.interfaces: HarnessContext.signal: optional AbortSignal; at most one memoized session.abort() promise. Snapshot artifact key iceSessionJsonl stores unmodified UTF-8 native session JSONL before directory removal. Cleanup order: snapshot → dispose → recursive force rm; error order preserves original run error before cleanup errors. Successful timings.totalMs includes setup, prompts/reloads, output projection and cleanup.
entries.dependency_text: The application session supplies abort/dispose semantics through MISC-041's SDK prerequisites. MISC-044 consumes the saved snapshot; do not reverse that dependency or write the artifact after deleting the workspace.
entries.rust: Native AgentLane::abort cancels the active signal on the current lane and returns an AbortResult; it rejects for a closed harness, another active lane or no active run. It does not itself await completion. wait_for_idle is a distinct operation. close sets the closed flag and cancels the child scope; its own source does not implement an eval snapshot/remove transaction (rust:crates/ice-harness/src/agent_harness.rs:4636-4666; rust:crates/ice-harness/src/agent_harness.rs:4882-4914; rust:crates/ice-harness/src/agent_harness.rs:2039-2047). These primitives are partial support, not equivalent to the eval adapter's memoized abort, snapshot and aggregated cleanup sequence.
entries.port: Use a scoped eval-run owner that records the primary outcome and independently attempts snapshot, session shutdown and temporary-root removal in that order. Map native cancellation to an explicit wait for the run/shutdown operation where needed, because native abort only signals. Preserve all cleanup errors and stable ordering in an aggregate error type. Keep the source's phase boundaries visible in compatibility behavior; any stronger cancellation guarantees during model initialization or reload should be documented and tested separately. Add future targeted failure-injection cases for snapshot failure, disposal failure, removal failure, abort rejection and a primary-plus-cleanup error.
entries.priority_reason: Evaluation failures must retain useful session evidence and reliably release temporary resources without concealing the original error.

entries.title: Strict prompt completion, normalized transcripts and evaluation usage
entries.what: The eval result contains a strict successful response, a normalized message/tool trace and session token/cost telemetry suitable for judges and paired comparisons.
entries.mechanism:
A prompt succeeds only when the newly appended messages include an assistant whose final stop reason is exactly 'stop' and the session exposes nonempty assistant text. The adapter then projects the complete session into evaluation events. It reports session-wide usage while retaining the initially selected model's identity and pricing gate.

promptAgent checks abort, records the current message count, awaits session.prompt(input), and searches the newly appended suffix backwards for an assistant. Missing assistant rejects. Any stopReason other than 'stop' rejects with errorMessage when non-nullish, otherwise 'Agent run ended with unexpected stop reason: <reason>.'. An explicitly empty errorMessage is retained by ??, not replaced. It obtains the response with getLastAssistantText() and rejects a falsy result; whitespace-only text remains truthy and is not trimmed here. The smoke scenario separately trims its own final assertion (ice:packages/evals/src/ice-harness.ts:90-107).

contentText returns a string unchanged or joins only text blocks with newline. For each user message, the transcript emits a user message event even if the extracted text is empty. For assistants it emits one nonempty combined text message, then one tool_call per toolCall content block in original tool-call order, with id/name and arguments delegated to external normalizeRecord. This groups all assistant text before its tool calls rather than preserving interleaving among original content blocks. Thinking and image blocks are not independent assistant trace events. A toolResult emits tool_result with toolCallId/name; all-text content becomes the combined string, otherwise the entire content array goes through external toJsonValue. Error results add error.message equal to the extracted text or 'Tool failed'. Other application message roles are ignored by this projection (ice:packages/evals/src/ice-harness.ts:58-88; ice:packages/ai/src/utils/text.ts:1-13).

After awaiting the optional output projection, getSessionStats supplies input/output/total tokens, toolCalls, cache-read/write counts and aggregate cost. usage.provider/model come from the initially selected model. estimatedCostUsd is included only when that model's base cost or any tier has a positive input/output/cacheRead/cacheWrite price; zero/absent pricing remains unavailable instead of being reported as an observed zero-dollar cost. The gate checks positive values, not price completeness. Token/cost counters cover whatever the session accumulated before this point; the adapter does not recompute them from its lossy normalized transcript or rebind identity if an extension/output callback changes the session model. Successful totalMs is attached later after cleanup under MISC-042 (ice:packages/evals/src/ice-harness.ts:178-203).

createHarness, normalizeRecord and toJsonValue belong to the pinned external vitest-evals dependency. This audit reads their checked-in invocation contracts, not that dependency's implementation; no invented normalization/error serialization guarantees are credited to the local adapter.
entries.interfaces: SimpleHarnessResult output:string|JsonValue; events:{type:'message',role,content}|{type:'tool_call',id,name,arguments}|{type:'tool_result',toolCallId,name,content,error?}. usage:{provider,model,inputTokens,outputTokens,totalTokens,toolCalls,metadata:{cacheReadTokens,cacheWriteTokens,estimatedCostUsd?}}. Empty/failing outputs reject rather than becoming a scored answer. Snapshot JSONL remains a separate full-fidelity artifact.
entries.dependency_text: SESSION-027 owns aggregate usage accounting; this entry owns its eval representation and the selected-model pricing gate. Shared provider/message schemas remain upstream prerequisites, not duplicate estimated work.
entries.rust: Native prompt_text constructs a UserMessage and calls the real run loop; its result distinguishes Completed, Aborted, Failed and Suspended with persisted IDs and messages. get_stats delegates to the session view. The inspected deterministic tests assert a two-turn tool run and a one-turn text response, durable messages and provider call counts (rust:crates/ice-harness/src/agent_harness.rs:4526-4546; rust:crates/ice-harness/tests/harness_run_e2e.rs:205-454). However derive_outcome treats Error, Aborted and Deferred specially and maps the remaining stop reasons to Completed; Completed alone therefore does not establish the eval adapter's exact Stop requirement (rust:crates/ice-harness/src/agent_harness.rs:3428-3502). No matching normalized evaluation trace/usage adapter was found. Preserve native outcome detail and session messages rather than replacing them with the reduced trace.
entries.port: Add a strict eval result adapter that inspects the final newly generated assistant and accepts only Stop with nonempty exposed text. Translate complete session messages using the exact text aggregation, tool ID/error and mixed-content rules, while preserving native JSONL separately. Reuse session stats and include estimated cost only when the selected model has a positive base/tier price. Keep unavailable cost distinct from zero. Decide and document any deliberate improvement to model identity when a scenario switches models; compatibility behavior currently labels the initially selected model. Future tests should cover missing assistant, length/abort/deferred outcomes, empty versus whitespace text, mixed tool-result content, interleaved assistant text/tools and unpriced models.
entries.priority_reason: Judges and comparisons require stable trace semantics and must not treat truncated/error responses or unknown cost as successful measured data.

entries.title: Task-bound session/source artifacts and scoped attachment persistence
entries.what: Evaluation runs attach their native session JSONL and generated source to the explicit test task, then persist only attachments belonging to the reported run.
entries.mechanism:
Session snapshots are captured before workspace removal and registered on the actual Vitest task after each eval. The reporter persists selected session/source attachments into separate run-scoped directories. Run IDs are hashed for directory names, while the attachment basename is checked before writing.

ICE_SESSION_SNAPSHOT_ARTIFACT is the literal artifact key 'iceSessionJsonl'. recordEvalSessionArtifact receives an explicit Readonly<RunnerTestCase> and a run's artifact map. An undefined snapshot returns without validating runId; a present snapshot requires both runId and session to be strings or throws TypeError('Ice eval session artifact metadata is invalid.'). It records type '@zykairotis/ice-evals:session', the run ID and one attachment named session.jsonl with application/jsonl, UTF-8 body and bodyEncoding='utf-8'. The eval-only afterEach hook reads task.meta.harness?.run and calls this function when a run exists. It does not rely on an implicit currently running test during reporter execution (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/artifacts.ts:13-73; ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/setup.ts:1-9).

recordEvalSourceArtifact records type '@zykairotis/ice-evals:source', a supplied runId and one SourceAttachment. Its TypeScript interface specifies name, contentType, string body and UTF-8 encoding, but this wrapper adds no runtime validation. Unique module-local symbols extend Vitest's TestArtifactRegistry for the two record types; the wire discriminator remains the string type.

persistEvalArtifactReferences walks artifacts in order and selects only these two types whose runId strictly equals the report run ID. It chooses sessions or sources by type. For each attachment it computes basename(name), rejects when that differs from the original name, creates <artifactDirectory>/<category>/<SHA-256(runId)> recursively with requested mode0700, and writes the body as UTF-8 using requested mode0600. The returned ordered references contain only {name,path}, with path relative to artifactDirectory. These checks use the host's basename semantics; they do not add a platform-independent path grammar or reject dot/empty basenames in advance. Such names can still fail at write time. Repeated same-category/run/name writes overwrite the same path and can yield repeated references; there is no content deduplication, exclusive-create option or rollback transaction. Mode arguments apply to creation and do not force a chmod of preexisting paths (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/artifacts.ts:87-112).

The direct suite was fully read: it checks explicit-task registration, run/type filtering, 64-hex run directories and exact persisted contents. It does not cover malformed attachment names, overwrite collisions or injected I/O failures. Session/source contents are retained unredacted by this helper, matching the README's description of prompts/responses/source/tool-output artifacts.
entries.interfaces: Artifact types '@zykairotis/ice-evals:session' and '@zykairotis/ice-evals:source'; runId:string; attachments:[{name,contentType,body,bodyEncoding:'utf-8'}]|[]. Snapshot key iceSessionJsonl. Paths sessions/<sha256(runId)>/session.jsonl and sources/<sha256(runId)>/<basename>. recordEvalSessionArtifact(task,run), recordEvalSourceArtifact(task,runId,attachment), persistEvalArtifactReferences(artifacts,runId,artifactDirectory).
entries.dependency_text: MISC-042 provides the pre-cleanup snapshot. This entry owns the task/attachment protocol and persistence, while native session storage remains the SESSION area's existing capability.
entries.rust: Native session JSONL storage is real and independently audited in SESSION; its public module exports codec/repository/storage/types (rust:crates/ice-harness/src/session/jsonl/mod.rs:1-27). The inspected e2e test asserts persisted entry and operation chains. Neither native persistence nor those assertions establish the eval-specific task registry, source attachment type, hashed run directory/reference protocol or afterEach handoff. Reused SESSION full-read credit for JSONL modules is recorded separately in the source review, not presented as this worker independently rereading all storage code.
entries.port: Define native evaluation attachment records with explicit run/task identity and separate session/source categories. Snapshot native session bytes before cleanup, register them on the test result and persist only matching-run attachments using the defined hashed-directory/reference layout. Preserve native JSONL format rather than reserializing the reduced trace. Validate attachment basenames at the boundary; any stronger cross-platform or dot-name rejection should be documented as a safety correction to the current helper. Future tests should retain the source suite's run selection and exact byte checks and add collision and I/O failure behavior.
entries.priority_reason: Failed model workflows need durable, correctly associated evidence after their temporary projects have been removed.

entries.title: Comparative harness tables, canonical input pairing and failure metadata
entries.what: A comparison declares one baseline and one or more candidates, repeats them in a stable order and attaches a deterministic input/repetition identity to every wrapped run, including recoverable partial failures.
entries.mechanism:
The table generates baseline-then-candidate rows for each repetition. Inputs are paired by a trimmed explicit string ID when available, otherwise by a hash of strict canonical JSON. Iteration metadata is attached before execution and merged into successful or externally attached partial runs.

Options accept either candidate or candidates with a baseline and optional repetitions. The implementation chooses the singular property when 'candidate' in options, otherwise uses the candidate array. Default repetitions is1. validateOptions rejects a whitespace-only evalSet, zero candidates, duplicate exact harness.name values and repetitions that are not a positive safe integer. It does not trim stored evalSet/names or independently reject an empty harness name. Rows enumerate repetitions1..N, with baseline first then candidates in declaration order. The builder does not randomize or schedule execution; callers use describe.for and may independently configure Vitest sequencing (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/harness-table.ts:114-128; ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/harness-table.ts:157-193).

deriveInputKey first checks non-null, non-array object inputs with an 'id' property, including an inherited property. A nonempty trimmed string ID is returned directly and bypasses validation of all other input fields. Otherwise canonicalizeJson accepts null/string/boolean and finite numbers, dense arrays with an own property at every numeric index, and only Object.prototype/null-prototype objects. It rejects other primitive types, non-finite numbers, sparse arrays, cycles and non-plain object prototypes. Object.entries selects enumerable own string-keyed fields, sorts keys lexically with < and >, recursively canonicalizes values and reconstructs an object before JSON.stringify. The WeakSet tracks ancestors and deletes on return, so repeated noncyclic object references are allowed. SHA-256 of that canonical JSON string becomes a lower-case hex input key. The final group key is JSON.stringify([inputKey,repetition]); explicit IDs and hash keys share the same string namespace (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/harness-table.ts:66-112).

Each wrapper sets artifact 'vitestEvalsHarnessIteration' before calling the underlying harness. The artifact is {schemaVersion:1,evalSet,groupKey,harness,baseline,candidates,repetition}. On success, it mutates run.artifacts by merging context.artifacts, then existing run.artifacts, then the authoritative iteration value. On failure it asks external getHarnessRunFromError for a partial run; when present it performs the same merge and rethrows through attachHarnessRunToError. Errors without an attached run are rethrown unchanged. A group-key error happens before the artifact is set (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/harness-table.ts:130-155).

The parser is intentionally less strict than the table builder: it requires a non-array object, schemaVersion===1, the named string fields, an array of string candidate names and typeof repetition==='number'. It does not require finite/positive/integer repetition, nonempty strings, unique candidates or baseline/harness membership. The direct tests cover canonical key order, trimmed IDs, array order, unsupported/sparse/cyclic inputs, row order, singular candidate and success metadata. They do not assert all builder/parser validation branches or the partial-error attachment path.
entries.interfaces: evalHarnessTable(evalSet,{baseline,candidate|candidates,repetitions?}) -> [{harness,name,repetition}]. deriveEvalGroupKey(input,repetition):string. EVAL_HARNESS_ITERATION_ARTIFACT='vitestEvalsHarnessIteration'. parseEvalHarnessIterationArtifact(JsonValue|undefined) -> schemaVersion1 record|undefined. Error attachment helpers are consumed from external vitest-evals, not locally implemented.
entries.dependency_text: This generic comparison layer is independent of ICE session construction. MISC-046 reads its artifact and MISC-047 aggregates observations; those are consumers, not prerequisites.
entries.rust: The inspected native public harness module and deterministic test helper support constructing/running a harness but contain no baseline/candidate table, canonical input key, repetition artifact or partial-run error attachment protocol. No matching comparative-eval symbols appeared in the bounded crate search. Existing native session/run IDs remain useful runtime identities but are not a substitute for a cross-harness input/repetition pairing key.
entries.port: Implement a generic native comparison plan and versioned iteration artifact, retaining exact declaration/repetition order and authoritative metadata merge. Port canonical JSON hashing with deliberate handling of the explicit-ID fast path and repeated noncyclic references; for serde_json inputs, document which JavaScript-only invalid cases become unrepresentable. Preserve the parser's current acceptance boundary or publish a versioned stricter schema rather than silently claiming validation parity. Attach iteration identity to both successful runs and available partial failures so reporting can diagnose missing/error observations. Add future tests for duplicate names, invalid repetitions, malformed artifacts and error-path metadata in addition to the read suite.
entries.priority_reason: Comparisons are misleading unless the same input and repetition are paired consistently and failures retain their intended treatment identity.

entries.title: Per-test run index, observation extraction and interrupted-run reporting
entries.what: The eval reporter appends a compact index for each completed harness-bearing test and derives comparison observations from explicit iteration metadata and judge scores.
entries.mechanism:
A per-test callback persists attachments and appends a JSONL run record when an artifact directory is configured. A separate end-of-run pass derives observations from test metadata and prints the paired comparison report. An interrupted run suppresses that aggregate comparison without erasing already written per-test records.

appendHarnessRunReport trims ICE_EVAL_ARTIFACT_DIR and returns when absent or empty. Unlike the runner, this function does not resolve the value relative to the eval package root. It requires test.meta().harness and external isHarnessRun(harness.run). A string run.artifacts.runId is retained, including an empty string; otherwise a UUID is generated. Metadata copies every run artifact except runId and iceSessionJsonl. The record is schemaVersion1 with runId; test{id,file:relativeModuleId,name,fullName,status}; harness name; usage; optional timings; nonempty errors; persisted attachment references; and nonempty metadata. It does not directly serialize the output, normalized transcript or test.meta().eval.avgScore into this local index (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/reporter.ts:14-44).

Attachment persistence happens before creating the root and appending runs.jsonl. The root is requested recursively with mode0700; appendFile uses UTF-8, flag'a' and mode0600. There is no local index deduplication, file lock, whole-record transaction with attachments, or recovery rollback. I/O errors propagate from the awaited callback; attachments may exist even when the later index append fails. Other reporters may emit their own formats, but those external formats are not inferred here (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/reporter.ts:42-50; ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/reporter.ts:96-98).

collectHarnessObservations enumerates every module's allTests, requires a recognized harness run and a successfully parsed vitestEvalsHarnessIteration artifact, and copies evalSet/groupKey/harness/baseline/candidates/repetition. Pairing uses module.relativeModuleId and test.name, not fullName. avgScore and estimatedCostUsd are accepted only when typeof number and finite. totalTokens and totalMs are copied when not undefined; the summary later rejects non-finite metric pairs. If run.errors is nonempty, outcome is errored even when a judge score exists. Otherwise a finite judge score creates a scored observation regardless of the Vitest result state. Without a score, passed becomes unscored, failed becomes errored, and other test states pass through. A failed hard assertion with an existing finite score and no harness-run error is therefore still scored for this comparison, although Vitest may fail the test (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/reporter.ts:53-87).

onInit stores the Vitest logger. onTestRunEnd ignores its serialized-error argument; reason==='interrupted' prints the unavailable message and returns. Other end reasons summarize and format the collected observations, printing only nonempty output. Tests that never produced a recognized harness run or iteration artifact are not synthesized into observations; a missing counterpart can only be diagnosed where another observed run declares the comparison. The local inventory has no dedicated reporter unit suite, so these branches are source-read only.
entries.interfaces: EvalHarnessReporter hooks onInit, async onTestCaseResult, onTestRunEnd. Environment ICE_EVAL_ARTIFACT_DIR. runs.jsonl schemaVersion1 fields: runId,test,harness,usage,timings?,errors?,artifacts,metadata?. Test metadata inputs harness.run and eval.avgScore. Outcome precedence: harness errors → finite score → mapped test state. Interrupted message: 'Eval comparisons unavailable: test run interrupted.'.
entries.dependency_text: The reporter consumes normalized runs, persisted attachments, iteration identity and the independent summary algorithm. External vitest-evals run recognition and judge metadata are pinned dependency boundaries; no local implementation is invented for them.
entries.rust: Native harness tests inspect durable operation_started/operation_finished records and RunStart/RunEnd events, so native run identity and completion evidence are present (rust:crates/ice-harness/tests/harness_run_e2e.rs:336-396). Those records are runtime telemetry, not this test-task index or observation collector. The bounded native module/symbol inventory found no matching eval reporter, judge-score/test-state precedence or interrupted aggregate-output policy.
entries.port: Add a native reporter layer that associates each test with its harness run, persists matching attachments and appends the versioned index. Preserve the distinction between test status, harness errors and measured judge score; do not infer correctness from a passed test or silently count an unexecuted run. Keep local index fields explicit and treat failed I/O as a reporter failure. If durable score replay is desired, extend/version the schema rather than claiming the present index already stores judge scores. Add future tests for missing metadata, fallback run IDs, error-versus-score precedence, failed assertion with a score, interrupted runs and an attachment/index partial failure.
entries.priority_reason: Reliable comparison output depends on correct association of tests, artifacts, errors and scores; runtime telemetry alone cannot supply these semantics.

entries.title: Paired correctness lift, telemetry availability and diagnostic terminal summaries
entries.what: Comparison summaries pair each declared candidate only with its baseline, calculate correctness separately from efficiency, and expose missing/duplicate/error observations instead of filling them with zero.
entries.mechanism:
The summary uses matched observations for the same file, test name, input key and repetition. Correctness is the difference in pass rates, while tokens, latency and estimated cost are separate paired metrics. Missing scores or telemetry remain unavailable and contribute explicit coverage or diagnostics.

groupObservations groups first by evalSet. The first observation fixes that set's baseline; later conflicting baseline declarations are not validated. Candidate names are unioned, retaining their smallest observed declaration index. Each group key is JSON.stringify([file,testName,groupKey]); the stored repetition and other group labels come from the first observation, so repetition only affects grouping independently when already encoded by the table's groupKey. Runs with the same file, leaf test.name and input key can collide even if their fullName differs. Observations are stored as arrays per harness, retaining duplicates. Candidates sort by retained index then localeCompare name; eval sets sort by localeCompare, groups by groupKey then repetition (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/summary.ts:112-161).

Every group and declared harness is diagnosed once with this precedence: zero observations→missing-observation; more than one→duplicate-observation; one errored→harness-error; one unscored→missing-score; one other non-scored outcome→unscorable-outcome. Diagnostics are shared across all candidate comparisons and finally sort by evalSet,file,groupKey,repetition,harness; they are not duplicated for each pair. Each candidate is paired only with the declared baseline, and only groups with exactly one observation for each side become candidate pairs. totalPairs is all groups in the eval set, including groups with missing or duplicate data (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/summary.ts:164-210; ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/summary.ts:284-328).

Correctness includes a pair only when both outcomes are scored. A score>=1 is a pass; no rounding, clamping or fractional-credit pass threshold is substituted. Baseline/candidate wins mean only one side passes; ties mean both pass or both fail. Pass rates divide by eligiblePairs; zero eligible pairs yields null rates and lift. Lift is candidateRate-baselineRate, rounded through Number(difference.toPrecision(15)). The public summary function itself does not revalidate score finiteness; its normal reporter caller filters scores under MISC-046. Metrics likewise require two scored observations and two defined finite values, independently for totalTokens,totalMs,estimatedCostUsd. Negative finite values are not rejected by this helper. It computes each side's mean over that metric's eligible pairs and the same 15-significant-digit candidate-minus-baseline difference. No value is imputed for missing telemetry, and no confidence interval or significance test is computed (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/summary.ts:104-110; ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/summary.ts:212-281).

Formatting returns empty when every eval set has no comparisons, even if a manually supplied report has diagnostics. Otherwise it prints 'Eval Comparisons', set names, right-aligned9-character labels, baseline and candidate names and correctness eligible/total pair counts. Pass rates use one decimal percent and lift uses signed one-decimal percentage points. Tokens and milliseconds use one decimal; estimated USD uses four. Positive correctness is green, negative correctness red; lower efficiency metrics are green, higher red; zero deltas gray and unavailable values yellow. Metric coverage is appended only for a nonzero eligible count that differs from correctness eligiblePairs; a wholly unavailable metric has no separate zero-pair suffix. Incomplete observations follow with reason,file/testName,repetition,harness. Styling uses Node styleText; terminal color emission policy is not reimplemented locally (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/summary.ts:330-438).

The full direct suite covers correctness versus efficiency, missing observations/telemetry, file separation, harness-error and unscored exclusion, baseline-only candidate comparisons, declared missing harnesses, deduplicated diagnostics and terminal strings. These assertions were inspected only; no model/test execution or statistical result was produced.
entries.interfaces: HarnessObservation outcomes scored{score},unscored,skipped,pending,errored. HarnessComparisonReport{schemaVersion:1,evalSets:[{evalSet,comparisons}],diagnostics}. Each comparison has correctness{totalPairs,eligiblePairs,baselinePassRate,candidatePassRate,lift,baselineWins,candidateWins,ties} and three PairedMetricSummary records{totalPairs,eligiblePairs,baselineMean,candidateMean,meanDelta}. summarizeHarnessComparisons(observations); formatHarnessComparisonReport(report).
entries.dependency_text: MISC-045 defines the intended input/repetition identity. This mathematical/report-format layer does not depend on the reporter that consumes it. Native session statistics are inputs supplied by MISC-043 rather than duplicate work here.
entries.rust: Native get_stats and the audited session usage layer supply runtime aggregates, but the inspected native public harness/test surfaces have no cross-harness pairing, scored-observation model, null-aware lift/metric summaries or this comparison display. Do not treat ordinary token totals or test pass/fail counts as equivalent to paired judge-score comparisons.
entries.port: Implement the versioned observation/report types and deterministic grouping, duplicate handling and baseline pairing. Preserve the source's eligible-pair denominators, exact score>=1 rule, unavailable null values and separate per-metric eligibility. Match the rounding/formatting where results must compare byte-for-byte, while allowing native styling to carry equivalent semantic colors. Explicitly validate or version any stronger treatment of conflicting baselines, malformed repetition or non-finite direct-call scores; those checks are absent from the current helper. Port the read deterministic fixtures, including the +100.0pp and -4159.5ms formatting case, without running real models to test summary arithmetic.
entries.priority_reason: Unpaired or zero-filled summaries could misstate whether a prompt, tool or model change improved measured behavior.

entries.title: Built-in smoke and extension-authoring evaluation scenarios
entries.what: The shipped suites exercise a real selected model and a create/reload/use extension workflow, comparing prompt variants with an all-or-nothing behavioral judge while retaining source/session evidence.
entries.mechanism:
The smoke suite checks one no-tools answer and basic model telemetry. The extension suite compares two system-prompt variants on the same two-prompt workflow with an intervening resource reload. Its judge records task correctness, while hard assertions protect the intended prompt-treatment setup.

The smoke harness uses noTools='all' and the default harness/model selection. It asks for the capital of France, requires output.trim()==='Paris', result.errors===[], usage.provider/model equal the ICE_PROVIDER/ICE_MODEL environment values and totalTokens>0. It supplies no iteration table or judge, so the local comparison collector ignores it, though its recognized harness run can still be indexed. The runner may launch with no model defaults, but executing this shipped default-model smoke test still fails selection unless defaults exist; the no-default allowance applies when selected harnesses configure their own model (ice:packages/evals/src/smoke.eval.ts:1-18; ice:packages/evals/scripts/run-evals.mjs:49-63).

createExtensionAuthoringHarness projects the response, markers for Guidelines and ICE documentation in the effective system prompt, resource-loader errors, each loaded extension path/tool-name list and the UTF-8 source at <session cwd>/.ice/extensions/hello.ts when it exists. The baseline 'system-prompt-without-docs' truncates the default prompt at the first '\nGuidelines:\n' and throws if absent. Candidate 'default-system-prompt' removes the last '\nCurrent working directory: ' suffix and throws if absent. The two transforms are not arbitrary whole-section parsers; they use these exact string markers and slices. evalHarnessTable uses its default one repetition with baseline then candidate (ice:packages/evals/src/extensions.eval.ts:18-51; ice:packages/evals/src/extensions.eval.ts:100-103).

Both runs ask the model to create a hello tool accepting a name, reload the session, then ask it to call the tool for Bob and respond with exactly the greeting. The source path is a fixed expected hello.ts even though the first prompt does not explicitly name that file. The judge fails when that source is unavailable. It extracts imports with a regex matching from/import followed by whitespace and a quoted specifier; this is not a TypeScript parser and does not inspect dynamic import(...) forms. It requires a canonical @zykairotis/ice-coding-agent import, rejects matched @mariozechner/* or @sinclair/typebox* imports, requires zero loader errors and a loaded 'hello' tool, and requires a normalized successful call named hello with arguments.name==='Bob' and result==='Hello, Bob!'. Final response must equal 'Hello, Bob!' exactly without trimming. All conditions must pass for score1; otherwise score0 with semicolon-joined rationale metadata (ice:packages/evals/src/extensions.eval.ts:53-98).

describeEval receives that judge and judgeThreshold:null, expressing observational scoring rather than a score threshold gate. The test records hello.ts as a text/typescript UTF-8 source artifact when source exists, requiring a string runId first. It then hard-asserts that Guidelines/documentation markers match whether the harness name is 'default-system-prompt'. The README directs comparative suites to use judges for correctness and hard assertions only for setup/infrastructure invariants; it states that expect.soft still fails a test. That external framework behavior is not independently executed here. Four local unit suites test helper contracts, while the two *.eval.ts files are model-backed scenarios whose outcomes remain unverified.
entries.interfaces: Suites 'Ice Coding Agent smoke' and 'Ice extension authoring system prompt'; judge ExtensionAuthoringJudge; harness names system-prompt-without-docs and default-system-prompt. Tool contract hello({name:'Bob'})→'Hello, Bob!'. Expected source .ice/extensions/hello.ts; canonical module @zykairotis/ice-coding-agent, rejected legacy module prefixes. Extension projection includes response,systemPromptHasGuidelines,systemPromptHasIceDocs,extensionErrors,loadedExtensions,extensionSource.
entries.dependency_text: The eval infrastructure entries own execution/artifacts/comparisons. Extension discovery/loading/driver and session reload remain prerequisites; this entry owns scenario inputs, output projection and correctness criteria only. Native runtime branding/path choice follows the active fork's SET-001 contract rather than mechanically creating an obsolete user directory.
entries.rust: The native harness_run_e2e tests are substantial deterministic coverage: a caller-supplied Faux script executes real read/write/bash tool implementations against in-memory state, checks a write and its durable message/operation chain, verifies run events, and checks a single-turn response. Those complete relevant test bodies were read at1–454 and retained as existing capability. They use no real model or generated extension source and have no prompt-treatment comparison or ExtensionAuthoringJudge. Native extension packaging/runtime is separately credited under EXT; it is not an executed model-authoring evaluation. No outcome of either TypeScript or Rust suite was measured during this audit.
entries.port: Port the no-tools smoke and create/reload/use behavior into the explicit native eval command, using native model/auth selection and the shared run/artifact contracts. Preserve the deterministic Faux tests as fast infrastructure checks. For an extension-authoring comparison, choose the actual supported native extension source/ABI and active runtime directory, then encode its canonical import/registration rules and retain generated source artifacts; do not claim TS hello.ts loading parity from native plugin tests. Keep treatment-marker assertions separate from measured judge scores, state the repetition count, and record model/provider/session identity. Validate helper behavior with local fixtures before opting into authenticated model runs.
entries.priority_reason: These scenarios measure the end-to-end behaviors the evaluation infrastructure is intended to compare; helper tests alone do not establish real-model or extension-authoring outcomes.
